title: AffordanceVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model Empowering Action Generation through Affordance-Aware Understanding
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models leverage the rich world knowledge of pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) to enable instruction-following robotic manipulation. However, the structural mismatch between VLM semantic spaces and embodied control policies often hinders the learning of precise perception-action mappings. To address this challenge, we propose AffordanceVLA, a scalable, unified framework that introduces structured affordance learning as a task-oriented and object-centric intermediate representation to establish a more precise and robust perception-action mapping. Specifically, we progressively model manipulation priors through three complementary components - Which2Act, Where2Act, and How2Act - which jointly produce spatially grounded, semantically conditioned, and action-coupled intermediate representations, thereby naturally bridging vision, language, and action. We integrate these modules into a Mixture-of-Transformer (MoT) architecture and adopt a three-stage progressive training curriculum that leverages 8.8M affordance-centric grounding and pointing samples, translating scalable vision-language supervision into improved robotic manipulation. To overcome the scarcity of dense affordance labels in robotic datasets, we also develop a robust automated data augmentation pipeline. Extensive experiments on ID & OOD simulation and real-world demonstrate that AffordanceVLA outperforms strong VLA baselines across diverse manipulation scenarios, validating structured affordance learning as a scalable and robust bridge that integrates multi-source vision-language supervision while connecting pretrained VLM semantics to embodied robot control.
